rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur'an describes angels as honored, obedient servants who do not speak ahead of God; the Prophet is told to remember and worship as they do.
rows.anchor: بل عباد مكرمون لا يسبقونه بالقول وهم بأمره يعملون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Merit lies in the servant's pure nature and sincere submission disclosed by choosing obedience; strenuous obedience by a hypocrite or diseased heart has no value.
rows.anchor: لا قيمه للطاعه مع العلم بخباثة نفس المطيع وقبح سريرته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Angels' pure nature and worship are superior to human nature and works, which are mixed with desire, anger, hidden association, and the self; the reward humans seek is already theirs.
rows.anchor: فالقوام الملكي أفضل من القوام الإنساني والأعمال الملكية الخالصة لوجه الله أفضل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Humans can develop gradually toward a degree of nearness and perfection beyond the angels' initial endowment; the creation of Adam and knowledge of the names support that possibility.
rows.anchor: من المحتمل أن ينال عن استعداده مقاما من القرب وموطنا من الكمال فوق ما قد ناله الملك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The angels' prostration to Adam was submission to the perfection of humanity; Adam served as their qibla, representing humankind before the angels.
rows.anchor: أن السجدة إنما كان خضوعا منهم لمقام الكمال الإنساني ولم يكن آدم عليه السلام إلا قبلة لهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The day is the Resurrection, with an implied command to remember it; an imam is someone followed.
rows.anchor: اليوم يوم القيامة والظرف متعلق بمقدر أي اذكر يوم كذا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur'an calls God-appointed human guides imams and also calls leaders of disbelief imams.
rows.anchor: سمى الله سبحانه بهذا الاسم أفرادا من البشر يهدون الناس بأمر الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The word imam is also used for the Torah, possibly extending to other revealed law books, and for the Preserved Tablet.
rows.anchor: وسمى به أيضا التوراة كما في قوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Preserved Tablet cannot be the imam here because the verse assigns each people its own imam, whereas the Tablet is one and common to all.
rows.anchor: لم يصلح أن يكون المراد بالإمام في الآية اللوح لكونه واحدا لا اختصاص له بأناس دون أناس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The imam cannot mean a revealed book: the call includes people before Noah, while Noah's was the first revealed book containing a religious law.
rows.anchor: أن أول الكتب السماوية المشتملة على الشريعة هو كتاب نوح عليه السلام ولا كتاب قبله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The imam of each people is the one they followed, whether on truth or falsehood; the text may also be read as the God-appointed true imam.
rows.anchor: فالمتعين أن يكون المراد بإمام كل أناس من يأتمون به في سبيلى الحق والباطل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Followers of misguidance remain with their leaders at the Resurrection and are summoned alongside them, as Pharaoh leads his people to the Fire.
rows.anchor: أن أهل الضلال لا يفارقون أولياءهم المتبوعين يوم القيامة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The unqualified wording and the following verses point to leaders people actually adopted in worldly life, whether divinely appointed or not.
rows.anchor: أن الإمام المدعو به هو الذي اتخذه الناس إماما واقتدوا به في الدنيا لا من اجتباه الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse does not merely call communities by labels such as the people of Abraham or Pharaoh; that reading cannot explain the ensuing division by record and blindness.
rows.anchor: وليس كما يظن أنهم ينادون بأسماء أئمتهم فيقال يا أمة إبراهيم ويا أمة محمد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The summons brings people in the company of their imam: followers of a true imam receive their records in the right hand, while those blind to the true imam appear blind.
rows.anchor: ثم يأخذ من اقتدى بإمام حق كتابه بيمينه ويظهر عمى من عمي عن معرفة الإمام الحق

rows.speaker: المفسرون
rows.claim: One reported interpretation takes the imam to be scripture, so people are called as followers of the Torah, Gospel, or Qur'an; the author has already explained its problems.
rows.anchor: وللمفسرين في تفسير الإمام في الآية مذاهب شتى مختلفة منها أن المراد بالإمام الكتاب

rows.speaker: المفسرون
rows.claim: Another view makes the imam a prophet for the truthful and Satan or a leader of error for the false; it relies on ordinary usage despite the Qur'an's specialized usage.
rows.anchor: ومنها أن المراد بالإمام النبي لمن كان على الحق والشيطان وإمام الضلال لمبتغي الباطل

rows.speaker: المفسرون
rows.claim: A further view identifies the imam as the book of deeds, supposedly followed because it determines Paradise or Hell; the author says the record follows deeds and contains no final verdict.
rows.anchor: ومنها أن المراد كتاب أعمالهم فيقال يا أصحاب كتاب الخير ويا أصحاب كتاب الشر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A community's record cannot be the imam: the following reference to a single record delivered in the right hand does not fit a collective record.
rows.anchor: الظاهر في الفرد دون الجماعة

rows.speaker: المفسرون
rows.claim: A reported reading makes imam a plural of mother and has people called by their mothers; the wording is unsuitable, the plural is rare, and al-Kashshaf calls it an inventive interpretation.
rows.anchor: ومنها أن المراد به الأمهات - بجعل إمام جمعا لأم -

rows.speaker: المفسرون
rows.claim: Another reported reading takes imam broadly as anything followed, true or false, and understands the summons as followers staying with their leaders; the author rejects this generic sense in Qur'anic usage.
rows.anchor: ومنها أن المراد به المقتدى به والمتبع عاقلا كان أو غيره حقا كان أو باطلا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In Qur'anic usage an imam is either one who guides by God's command or a leader followed in error; a prophet guides as imam, while conveying revelation is his role as prophet or messenger.
rows.anchor: الإمام في عرف القرآن هو الذي يهدي بأمر الله أو المقتدى في الضلال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fatil is the fine thread in the groove of a date stone; another definition places it inside, while naqir is on its back and qitmir is its split husk.
rows.anchor: الفتيل هو المفتول الذي في شق النواة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The result following the summons shows that following the imam divides people into two groups: those given the record in the right hand and those who are blind.
rows.anchor: وتفريع التفصيل على دعوتهم بإمامهم دليل على أن ائتمامهم هو الموجب لانقسامهم إلى قسمين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The contrast between this life and the Hereafter means blindness in both is blindness of insight; the added phrase “more astray” confirms the spiritual sense.
rows.anchor: دليل على أن الإشارة بهذه إلى الدنيا كما أن كون الآية مسوقة لبيان التطابق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One who fails to recognize the true imam and follow the truth in worldly life will lack happiness and guidance to forgiveness and mercy in the Hereafter.
rows.anchor: ومن كان في هذه الحياه الدنيا لا يعرف الإمام الحق ولا يسلك سبيل الحق

rows.speaker: بعض المفسرين
rows.claim: Some commentators take “in this” to refer to worldly blessings and explain blindness as failing to know or thank God for them; the author rejects this reading.
rows.anchor: والمعنى ومن كان في هذه النعم التي رزقها أعمى لا يعرفها ولا يشكر الله

rows.speaker: بعض المفسرين
rows.claim: Some commentators make worldly blindness spiritual but the Hereafter's blindness physical; the author rejects the split, noting bodily blindness there can still return to inner blindness.
rows.anchor: وكذا ما ذكره بعضهم أن المراد بعمى الدنيا عمى البصيرة وبعمى الآخرة عمى البصر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The second “blind” carries a comparative sense, meaning more blind and further astray in the Hereafter, as the context supports.
rows.anchor: وظاهر بعض المفسرين أن الأعمى الثاني في الآية تفيد معنى التفضيل

rows.speaker: زيد بن علي
rows.claim: A report from Zayd ibn Ali, from his father, explains human honor through creation's preference for humans and their ability to raise food and drink to the mouth by hand.
rows.anchor: عن زيد بن علي عن أبيه عليه السلام في قوله { ولقد كرمنا بني آدم } يقول فضلنا بني آدم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The examples in the two reports are particular instances of human preference, as the first report itself concludes.
rows.anchor: وما في الروايتين من قبيل ذكر بعض المصاديق والدليل عليه قوله في آخر الرواية الأولى فهذا من التفضيل

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر عليه السلام
rows.claim: A report from Jabir says everything except the human was created bent over, while the human was created upright, as an example of human distinction.
rows.anchor: عن جابر عن أبي جعفر عليه السلام { وفضلناهم على كثير ممن خلقنا تفضيلا } قال خلق كل شيء منكبا غير الإنسان خلق منتصبا

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر عليه السلام
rows.claim: Al-Baqir says the Messenger, Ali, Hasan, Husayn, and each person's imam will come with their respective communities on the Day of Resurrection.
rows.anchor: عن الفضيل قال سألت أبا جعفر عليه السلام عن قول الله { يوم ندعوا كل أناس بإمامهم } قال يجيء رسول الله

rows.speaker: الصادق عليه السلام
rows.claim: A report says each community is called to the one it followed; the Prophet and his household go to the Prophet, and their followers go to them.
rows.anchor: عن الصادق عليه السلام ألا تحمدون الله؟ إنه إذا كان يوم القيامة يدعى كل قوم إلى من يتولونه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The report makes the Prophet the imam of the imams and witness of witnesses, and shows that being summoned by one's imam applies among the imams too.
rows.anchor: وفيه دلالة على أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم إمام الأئمة كما أنه شهيد الشهداء

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم
rows.claim: A report through al-Rida's ancestors says every people is summoned with the imam of its time, the Book of its Lord, and the Sunna of its Prophet.
rows.anchor: يدعى كل أناس بإمام زمانهم وكتاب ربهم وسنة نبيهم

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم
rows.claim: A parallel report from Ali repeats that each community is summoned with its imam of the time, its scripture, and its Prophet's Sunna.
rows.anchor: يدعى كل قوم بإمام زمانهم وكتاب ربهم وسنة نبيهم

rows.speaker: أبو عبد الله عليه السلام
rows.claim: A report says the earth is never without an imam who makes God's lawful and unlawful rulings clear, citing this verse; it also quotes the Prophet that dying without an imam is a death of ignorance.
rows.anchor: وفي تفسير العياشي عن عمار الساباطي عن أبي عبد الله عليه السلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The argument for the earth never lacking an imam is the verse's universal summons of all people.
rows.anchor: ووجه الاحتجاج بالآية عموم الدعوة فيها لجميع الناس

rows.speaker: أبو عبد الله عليه السلام
rows.claim: A report says God will ask whether justice requires each people to be joined with the one they chose; after they agree, they separate into their groups.
rows.anchor: قال إذا كان يوم القيامة قال الله أليس العدل من ربكم أن يولوا كل قوم من تولوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This report supports reading the summons as bringing people with their imam, rather than merely calling them by name.
rows.anchor: وفيه تأييد لما قدمنا أن المراد بالدعوه بالإمام احضارهم معه دون النداء بالاسم

rows.speaker: القمي
rows.claim: Al-Qummi glosses fatil as the thin membrane on the back of a date stone.
rows.anchor: قال قال الجلدة التي في ظهر النواة

rows.speaker: أبو عبد الله عليه السلام
rows.claim: Abu Abd Allah explains blindness as missing a divine obligation: Abu Basir heard of a man with ample means who kept postponing the Hajj until death prevented him from performing it.
rows.anchor: عن المثنى عن أبي عبد الله عليه السلام قال سأله أبو بصير وأنا أسمع فقال له رجل له مائة ألف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After arguing against denial of monotheism and resurrection, the passage recalls the polytheists' plots to turn the Prophet from revelation and expel him from Mecca; it warns him against yielding and them against expelling him.
rows.anchor: حيث أرادوا أن يفتنوا النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم عن بعض ما أوحي إليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage also directs the Prophet to prayer and seeking God's protection in his comings and goings, and announces that truth will prevail.
rows.anchor: وفي الآيات إيصاء النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم بالصلوات والالتجاء بربه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Inna is lightened, as shown by the lām in layafṭinūnaka; fitna means causing someone to slip or turning him aside, while khalīl means friend, with “need” a remote derivation.
rows.anchor: إن مخففة بدليل اللام في { ليفتنونك } والفتنة الإزلال والصرف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “What We revealed” is the Qur'an, including monotheism, denial of partners, and the upright way of life; the verse means the polytheists nearly diverted the Prophet into acting contrary to revelation.
rows.anchor: أن المراد بالذي أوحينا إليك القرآن بما يشتمل عليه من التوحيد ونفي الشريك والسيرة الصالحة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some occasion reports say the polytheists asked the Prophet not to criticize their gods and to distance himself from his poor, low-status followers so they could sit with him and hear him.
rows.anchor: أن المشركين سألوا النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم أن يكف عن ذكر آلهتهم بسوء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Divine strengthening means infallibility; the conditional wording says the Prophet did not even approach a slight inclination toward them, much less accept their request.
rows.anchor: هو العصمة الإلهية وجعل جواب لولا قوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The doubled life and death mean twice the punishment of this world and the next; the closing threat says no help could free him from it.
rows.anchor: فالمراد بضعف الحياة والممات المضاعف من عذاب الحياة والممات

rows.speaker: أبان بن تغلب
rows.claim: Aban ibn Taghlib explains the doubling as punishment whose pain is multiplied, adducing a poetic line in which ḍaʿf means painful torment.
rows.anchor: ونقل في المجمع عن أبان بن تغلب أن المراد بالضعف العذاب المضاعف ألمه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author introduces an unnamed poetic line to show that ḍaʿf can mean painful torment; the line itself follows in the next segment.
rows.anchor: والمعنى لأذقناك عذاب الدنيا وعذاب الآخرة وأنشد قول الشاعر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Istifzāz is to unsettle and move lightly; “the land” means Mecca, khilāf means after, and qalīl means a short time.
rows.anchor: الاستفزاز الإزعاج والتحريك بخفة وسهولة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Meccan polytheists nearly drove the Prophet from Mecca; had he left, they would have remained only briefly before being destroyed.
rows.anchor: وإن المشركين قاربوا أن يزعجوك من أرض مكة لإخراجك منها

rows.speaker: بعض المفسرين
rows.claim: Some identify the would-be expellers as Jews seeking to remove the Prophet from Medina, or as Jews and polytheists jointly seeking to drive him from Arabia; the author rejects this because the sura is Meccan and the Jewish conflict came later.
rows.anchor: وقيل هؤلاء الذين كادوا يستفزونه هم اليهود أرادوا أن يخرجوه من المدينة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “A practice” is attached to their short remaining time: God has a settled practice of destroying polytheists who expel their messenger, established for the messengers and never changed.
rows.anchor: وإنما نسبها إلى رسله لأنها مسنونة لأجلهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Taḥwīl means transferring something from one state to another; God applies the same unaltered rule to those who expel messengers.
rows.anchor: التحويل نقل الشيء من حال إلى حال

rows.speaker: مجمع البيان
rows.claim: Al-Ṭabrisī says dulūk is the sun's decline; al-Mubarrad takes it as the span from decline to sunset, while another view identifies it with sunset.
rows.anchor: قال في مجمع البيان الدلوك الزوال

rows.speaker: مجمع البيان
rows.claim: The lexicon explains “decline” through the observer rubbing the eyes at the sun's brightness, whether at its zenith or setting.
rows.anchor: وأصله من الدلك فسمي الزوال دلوكا لأن الناظر إليها يدلك عينيه

rows.speaker: مجمع البيان
rows.claim: Al-Ṭabrisī glosses ghasaq al-layl as the onset of darkness, while al-Raghib's lexicon gives its intense darkness.
rows.anchor: وقال فيه غسق الليل ظهور ظلامه

rows.speaker: أئمة أهل البيت عليهم السلام
rows.claim: Reports transmitted through the Shi'i routes interpret dulūk as noon's decline and nightfall as midnight, covering the four prayers from noon through night.
rows.anchor: والمروي عن أئمه أهل البيت عليهم السلام من طرق الشيعة تفسير دلوك الشمس بزوالها وغسق الليل بمنتصفه

rows.speaker: الشاعر
rows.claim: The cited line says the speaker spent the night in painful torment after Malik's death; it illustrates ḍaʿf as torment.
rows.anchor: لمقتل مالك إذ بان مني أبيت الليل في ضعف أليم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The interval from noon to midnight contains four daily prayers; adding the dawn prayer named Qur'an al-fajr completes the five obligatory prayers.
rows.anchor: إليها تتم الصلوات الخمس اليومية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qur'an al-fajr is grammatically coordinated with prayer and means the dawn prayer because it includes recitation; reports agree on this interpretation.
rows.anchor: والمراد به صلاة الصبح لما تشمل عليه من القراءة وقد اتفقت الروايات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Reports from both traditions agree that night and day angels witness the dawn prayer.
rows.anchor: بأنه يشهده ملائكة الليل وملائكة النهار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tahajjud literally relates to sleep and means waking to keep vigil after sleeping; “by it” refers either to the Qur'an or to the night portion implied, and nāfilah means an added prayer.
rows.anchor: التهجد من الهجود وهو النوم في الأصل ومعنى التهجد التيقظ والسهر بعد النوم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One grammatical view treats “of the night” as an exhortation and the following fa as an imperative particle, as in “so fear Me alone.”
rows.anchor: من قبيل الإغراء نظير قولنا عليك بالليل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse tells the Prophet to pray with Qur'an after sleeping for part of the night, as an additional prayer beyond his obligation.
rows.anchor: والمعنى واسهر بعض الليل بعد نومتك بالقرآن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Maqāman maḥmūdan may mean a praised act of raising, a place where God establishes him, or a place God grants him.
rows.anchor: من الممكن أن يكون المقام مصدرا ميميا وهو البعث فيكون مفعولا مطلقا ليبعثك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because the station is praised without qualification and benefits all, it is the great intercession for which all creation praises the Prophet; reports from both traditions agree.
rows.anchor: فسروا المقام المحمود بأنه المقام الذي يحمده عليه جميع الخلائق وهو مقام الشفاعة الكبرى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A truthful entry and exit mean every undertaking is genuine, with outward action matching inward belief and words matching deeds; this is the station of the truthful.
rows.anchor: أن يكون الدخول والخروج في كل أمر منعوتا بالصدق جاريا على الحقيقة من غير أن يخالف ظاهره باطنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The prayer asks God to manage the Prophet's affairs as He manages those of the truthful and to grant him supporting authority against false arguments, enemy plots, and satanic misguidance.
rows.anchor: اللهم تول أمري كما تتولى أمر الصديقين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The entry and exit are not limited to the Hijra to Medina and return for Mecca's conquest, or to entering the grave and leaving it at resurrection; the prayer is general, though its context concerns the mission.
rows.anchor: فلا وجه لما ذكره بعض المفسرين أن المراد بالدخول والخروج دخول المدينة بالهجرة والخروج منها إلى مكة للفتح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Zahūq means destruction and disappearance; announcing truth's arrival tells the polytheists to abandon hope of turning the Prophet from his mission.
rows.anchor: الزهوق هو الهلاك والبطلان يقال زهقت نفسه إذا خرجت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Falsehood cannot endure, as the comparison with a rootless, uprooted evil tree also shows.
rows.anchor: وفي الآية دلالة على أن الباطل لا دوام له

rows.speaker: مجمع البيان
rows.claim: An occasion report says polytheists told the Prophet to stop insulting their gods and dismiss his poor followers so they could sit with him and listen; it says he hoped they would convert.
rows.anchor: في المجمع في سبب نزول قوله تعالى

rows.speaker: سعيد بن نفير
rows.claim: Al-Durr al-Manthur transmits a similar account from Ibn Abi Hatim, from Sa'id ibn Nufayr.
rows.anchor: وروي في الدر المنثور عن ابن أبي حاتم عن سعيد بن نفير ما يقرب منه

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: A report says Quraysh leaders invited the Prophet to touch their idols so they would join his religion; the author says it contradicts the verses, which deny even nearing such an inclination.
rows.anchor: وأما ما روي عن ابن عباس أن أمية بن خلف وأبا جهل بن هشام ورجالا من قريش أتوا رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: A report says Thaqif asked the Prophet for a year to collect offerings for their idols before converting and breaking them, and that he considered granting the delay.
rows.anchor: وكذا ما رواه الطبري وابن مردويه عن ابن عباس أن ثقيفا قالوا للنبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم أجلنا سنة

rows.speaker: أبو عبد الله عليه السلام
rows.claim: An Ayyashi report says that at the conquest Quraysh asked the Prophet to leave an idol at al-Marwa; he felt embarrassed, then ordered it broken.
rows.anchor: وكذا ما في تفسير العياشي عن أبي يعقوب عن أبي عبد الله عليه السلام في الآية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: These and similar reports conflict with the Qur'an's apparent meaning: the Prophet could not intend such innovations, and the reported incidents occurred after Hijra although the sura is Meccan.
rows.anchor: فهذه روايات لا تلائم ظاهر الكتاب وحاشا رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم أن يهم بمثل هذه البدع

rows.speaker: علي بن محمد بن الجهم
rows.claim: Al-Rida tells al-Ma'mun that verses framed as warnings to the Prophet, including “if you associate” and this verse, address the Prophet but intend his community.
rows.anchor: وفي العيون بإسناده عن علي بن محمد بن الجهم عن أبي الحسن الرضا عليه السلام مما سأله المأمون

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that after this threat the Prophet prayed, “God, do not leave me to myself even for a moment.”
rows.anchor: قال إنه لما نزلت هذه الآية قال النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم

rows.speaker: علي بن الحسين عليه السلام
rows.claim: A report says the five prayers took their present form in Medina after Islam grew strong: seven units were added to the noon, afternoon, sunset, and night prayers, while dawn remained as prescribed in Mecca so night and day angels could witness it.
rows.anchor: وفي تفسير العياشي عن سعيد بن المسيب عن علي بن الحسين عليه السلام قال قلت له متى فرضت الصلاة

rows.speaker: مجمع البيان
rows.claim: Al-Ṭabrisī says the verse explains the obligation and times of the five prayers; he cites a supporting report through al-Ayyashi and Ubayd ibn Zurara.
rows.anchor: قال ففي الآية بيان وجوب الصلوات الخمس وبيان أوقاتها ويؤيد ذلك ما رواه العياشي بالإسناد عن عبيد بن زرارة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The continuation of Ubayd ibn Zurara's report from Abu Abd Allah divides the four prayers into two from noon to sunset and two from sunset to midnight, each pair in order.
rows.anchor: قال إن الله افترض أربع صلوات أول وقتها من زوال الشمس إلى انتصاف الليل

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود
rows.claim: Ibn Mas'ud reports that Gabriel came at the sun's decline and prayed the noon prayer with the Prophet.
rows.anchor: عن ابن مسعود قال قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم

rows.speaker: أبو الدرداء
rows.claim: Abu al-Darda reports the Prophet's recitation and explanation that God and the night and day angels witness the dawn prayer.
rows.anchor: عن أبي الدرداء قال قرء رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The interpretation of dawn recitation as witnessed by night and day angels is nearly mass-transmitted in both traditions; some reports add God's and the Muslims' witness.
rows.anchor: تفسير كون قرآن الفجر مشهودا في روايات الفريقين بشهادة ملائكة الليل وملائكة النهار يكاد يبلغ حد التواتر

rows.speaker: أبو عبد الله عليه السلام
rows.claim: A report says believers need the Prophet's intercession because they have sins and faults; the Prophet repeatedly prostrates, receives permission, and intercedes for them.
rows.anchor: وفي تفسير العياشي عن عبيد بن زرارة قال سئل أبو عبد الله عليه السلام

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم
rows.claim: A report about the Prophet's saying that he is the master of Adam's children describes him prostrating at Paradise's gate and repeatedly receiving permission to intercede and ask.
rows.anchor: قال وسأله رجل عن قول رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم أنا سيد ولد آدم ولا فخر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author notes that several Sunni reports also recount this intercession tradition.
rows.anchor: وفي معنى هذه الرواية عدة روايات من طرق أهل السنة عن النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The report's reference to people already burned means some people admitted to Hell.
rows.anchor: أي بعض من أدخل النار

rows.speaker: ابن عمر
rows.claim: Ibn Umar reports that the sun draws near, people appeal to Adam and Moses, then Muhammad intercedes, takes the ring of Paradise's gate, and is raised to the praised station.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عمر قال سمعت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم يقول

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: Abu Hurayra reports the Prophet's explanation that the praised station is intercession.
rows.anchor: عن أبي هريرة أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم قال

rows.speaker: سعد بن أبي وقاص
rows.claim: Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas reports that the Prophet identified the praised station as intercession.
rows.anchor: عن سعد بن أبي الوقاص قال سئل رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم عن المقام المحمود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Many reports support the preceding descriptions of the praised station and intercession.
rows.anchor: والروايات في المضامين السابقة كثيرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage returns to the Qur'an as a prophetic sign and source of blessing: it heals and benefits believers, increases wrongdoers' loss, and is a miracle; it then addresses their requests and the question about the Spirit.
rows.anchor: فبين في هذه الآيات أن القرآن شفاء ورحمة وبعبارة أخرى مصلح لمن صلحت نفسه ومخسر للظالمين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The particle min explains the preceding relative phrase: what is sent down as healing and mercy is the Qur'an itself.
rows.anchor: أي وننزل ما هو شفاء ورحمة وهو القرآن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling the Qur'an a cure implies spiritual illnesses: like the body, the heart has an original sound nature, correct beliefs and morals, and disorders that need treatment.
rows.anchor: وعد القرآن شفاء والشفاء إنما يكون عن مرض دليل على أن للقلوب أحوالا نسبة القرآن إليها نسبة الدواء الشافي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Heart sickness can coexist with ordinary faith and is distinct from outright disbelief or hypocrisy; it is doubt, instability, inclination to falsehood, and following desire, a deficiency relative to higher faith.
rows.anchor: ليس هذا المسمى مرضا إلا ما يختل به ثبات القلب واستقامة النفس من أنواع الشك والريب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur'an cures doubts and objections with decisive proofs, and treats the heart's other ailments through sound admonitions, stories, examples, promises, warnings, laws, and rulings.
rows.anchor: والقرآن الكريم يزيل بحججه القاطعة وبراهينه الساطعة أنواع الشكوك والشبهات المعترضة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: As mercy, the Qur'an restores what disease removed: it gives knowledge and certainty and noble states after clearing ignorance, doubt, and base traits; healing clears obstacles, while mercy clothes the heart in happiness.
rows.anchor: فالقرآن شفاء ورحمة للقلوب المريضة كما أنه هدى ورحمة للنفوس غير الآمنة من الضلال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wrongdoers are unbelievers broadly, not only polytheists; their disbelief is why the Qur'an increases their loss of the innate religion that was their original capital.
rows.anchor: فالمراد بالظالمين غير المؤمنين وهم الكفار دون المشركين خاصة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rejecting the Qur'an adds loss to the loss caused by disbelief; the phrasing “only loss” signals that any remaining innate gift is further depleted, while believers gain health and stability.
rows.anchor: يزيدهم خسارا على خسار ونقصا على نقص إن كانت عندهم بقية من موهبة الفطرة

rows.speaker: بعض المفسرين
rows.claim: Some commentators broaden healing to include bodily illness through blessing in reciting or writing Qur'anic verses; the author allows the possibility.
rows.anchor: أن المراد بالشفاء في الآية أعم من شفاء الأمراض الروحية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If bodily healing is included, both halves should be read consistently: Qur'an can heal believers and help repel enemies, thereby increasing oppressors' loss; attributing that loss to Qur'an is figurative, since it stems from their choice.
rows.anchor: لكن لو صح التعميم فليصح في الصدر والذيل جميعا فإنه كما يستعان به على دفع الأمراض والعاهات

rows.speaker: المفردات
rows.claim: Al-Raghib explains that aʿraḍa ʿannī means turning away while showing one's side; naʾā bi-janibihi means taking distance from God.
rows.anchor: وإذا قيل أعرض عني فمعناه ولى مبديا عرضه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Together, “turned away and kept his side distant” pictures a person's separation from God when blessed; some commentators also read it as arrogance and self-exaltation.
rows.anchor: يمثل حال الإنسان في تباعده وانقطاعه من ربه عندما ينعم عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When even slight harm touches a person, he despairs of good; evil is not directly attributed to God because it is relative to its bearer, while the universal order makes it incidental to greater good.
rows.anchor: ولم ينسب الشر إليه تعالى كما نسب النعمة تنزيها له تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ordinary people attach to visible causes during prosperity and forget gratitude; when harm removes those causes, they despair because they see no other source of good.
rows.anchor: اشتغل بظواهر الأسباب وأخلد إليها فنسينا فلم يذكرنا ولم يشكرنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This describes the socially conditioned person's ordinary state, unlike the innate or emergency state in which distress makes people forget apparent causes and turn back to God.
rows.anchor: فللإنسان حالان حال فطرية تهديه إلى الرجوع إلى ربه عند مس الضر ونزول الشر وحال عاديه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: There is no contradiction with verses where distress makes people turn to God: those describe the innate response when apparent causes fail, whereas 17:83 describes ordinary attachment to causes.
rows.anchor: ومن هنا يظهر أن لا منافاة بين هذه الآية والآيات الدالة على أن الإنسان إذا مسه الضر رجع إلى ربه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse follows the Qur'an's warning of increased loss by explaining that people forget God amid blessings and despair at harm.
rows.anchor: ويظهر أيضا وجه اتصال الآية بما قبلها وأنها متصلة بالآية السابقة من جهة ذيلها

rows.speaker: أفلاطون
rows.claim: Plato's account treats evil as privation: in killing, the evil is the victim's loss of life, not the swordsman's strength, the sharp blade, or the victim's capacity to be cut.
rows.anchor: نقل عن أفلاطون أن الشر عدم وقد بين ذلك بالأمثلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Cosmic evils are privations attached to events and thus have a share in occurrence; they relate to divine decree incidentally, not essentially.
rows.anchor: كانت أعداما مضافة لا عدما مطلقا فلها حظ من الوجود والوقوع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Absolute nonexistence is one kind of nonbeing; privation is a missing perfection in something suited to possess it, such as blindness in a being naturally capable of sight.
rows.anchor: وإما مضاف إلى ملكة وهو عدم كمال الوجود عما من شأنه ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A thing's lacking another possible essence, such as a plant lacking animal life, follows from essences and is not something created; privative defects such as illness and pain arise only in material things from limited capacity.
rows.anchor: وهذا النوع من العدم من لوازم الماهيات وهي اعتبارية غير مجعولة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's decree essentially wills the existence a thing can receive; the accompanying lack is due to incapacity or limited receptivity and is attributed to creation only incidentally.
rows.anchor: فالذي تعلقت به كلمة الإيجاد والإرادة الإلهية وشمله القضاء بالذات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Of five possible balances of good and evil, pure evil, evil-dominant, and equal cases do not occur; divine wisdom creates pure good and what has more good than evil, since omitting them would yield greater evil.
rows.anchor: ولا يوجد شيء من الثلاثة الأخيرة لاستلزامه الترجيح من غير مرجح أو ترجيح المرجوح على الراجح

rows.speaker: الرازي
rows.claim: Al-Razi says this discussion has no place for philosophers who treat God as a necessary cause rather than a voluntary agent; the author replies that necessity belongs to the effect and cannot compel its cause.
rows.anchor: وعن الإمام الرازي أنه لا محل لهذا البحث منهم بناء على ما ذهبوا إليه من كونه تعالى علة تامة

rows.speaker: صاحب روح المعاني
rows.claim: The author praises al-Alusi's fair account: the debate assumes whether God's will is indifferent between opposites, while philosophers say divine choice follows universal laws, wisdom, and visible or hidden interests.
rows.anchor: ولقد أنصف صاحب روح المعاني حيث أشار أولا إلى نظير ما تقدم من البحث

rows.speaker: الإمام
rows.claim: The quoted criticism says philosophers' discussion of evil is pointless because they posit necessary compulsion in divine acts, like fire necessarily burning; the author calls this biased because philosophers affirm choice and investigate evil to avoid positing two principles.
rows.anchor: إن الفلاسفة لما قالوا بالإيجاب والجبر في الأفعال فخوضهم في هذا المبحث من جملة الفضول والضلال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author says the criticism is biased: philosophers affirm divine choice, and examine how evil occurs because God is pure good and they must avoid the dualist claim of separate good and evil principles.
rows.anchor: ناش من التعصب لأن محققيهم يثبتون الاختيار

rows.speaker: المفردات
rows.claim: Al-Raghib derives shākila from a tether that restrains an animal and glosses it as a disposition that constrains a person to act in ways suited to it.
rows.anchor: من الشكل وهو تقييد الدابة، ويسمى ما يقيد به شكالا

rows.speaker: مجمع البيان
rows.claim: Al-Ṭabrisī glosses shākila as a path or way of life, comparing it to branching roads.
rows.anchor: وفي المجمع الشاكلة الطريقة والمذهب يقال هذا طريق ذو شواكل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other explanations derive shākila from likeness or from a person's form or configuration.
rows.anchor: وقيل الشاكلة من الشكل بفتح الشين بمعنى المثل وقيل إنها من الشكل بكسر الشين بمعنى الهيئة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Human action follows one's disposition: psychological traits shape conduct, and bodily temperament is linked to how quickly traits such as anger or appetite form.
rows.anchor: الآية الكريمة ترتب عمل الإنسان على شاكلته بمعنى أن العمل يناسبها ويوافقها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Temperamental tendencies do not make an act necessary; even where acting against one's nature is difficult, the action remains voluntary.
rows.anchor: فليس يخرج دعوة المزاج المناسب لملكة من الملكات أو عمل من الأعمال من حد الاقتضاء إلى حد العلية التامة
